'''Chao-Jun "C.-J." Li''', a Canadian chemist, is E. B. Eddy Professor of Chemistry, Distinguished James McGill Chair Professor, and Canada Research Chair in Green Chemistry at [[McGill University]], [[Montréal]]. He is known for his pioneering works in Green Solvent (organic reactions in water) and Green Syntheses (water/functional group-tolerating organometallics, [[Carbon–hydrogen bond activation |C-H activation]], HOME Chemistry, and [[photochemistry]]).

== Education ==
C.-J. Li was born in 1963, and obtained his BSc from [[Zhengzhou University]] (1979–1983), and completed his MSc. in organic synthesis at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (1985–1988) remotely with Prof. T.H. Chan (McGill University).<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2005|title=New Associate Editor – The Americas|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2005/gc/b500233h|journal=Green Chemistry|volume=7|issue=2|page=58|doi=10.1039/B500233H|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He then moved to McGill University (Montréal, Québec) to do his PhD (1989–1992) with Prof. T.H. Chan again (and discovered the [[indium-mediated allylation]] reaction in water) along with Prof. [[David Harpp]] (working on organosulfur/selenium/tellurium chemistry), and went on a [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council|NSERC]]-funded postdoc with Prof. [[Barry Trost]] at [[Stanford University]] in the United States (1992–1994) (and discovered the so-called phosphine-catalyzed [[γ-Addition Reaction]]).

== Career and research ==
C.-J. Li started as an assistant professor at [[Tulane University]] in 1994, and attained the title of Professor of Chemistry in 2000. He then moved in 2003 to McGill University, where he obtained a [[Canada Research Chair]] (Tier I) in [[Green chemistry|Green Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=1140|title=Canada Research Chairs |last=Government of Canada|first=Industry Canada |date=2012-11-29|website=www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca|access-date=2020-04-18}}</ref> He has also been the director of [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council|NSERC]] CREATE for Green Chemistry (2012–2018), the director of CFI Infrastructure for Green Chemistry and Green Chemicals (2008–2018)  and has been the co-director of the [[:fr:Fonds québécois de la recherche sur la nature et les technologies|FQRNT]] Center for Green Chemistry and Catalysis since 2009. He was the founding Co-Chair of the Canadian Green Chemistry and Engineering Network.

C.-J. Li's research encompasses various aspects of green chemistry applied to organic chemistry: [[organometallic]]s, [[catalysis]] (thermal and light-based). Most notably, he is known for introducing [[On water reaction|water as a Green Solvent]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Li|first=Chao-Jun|date=1993-09-01|title=Organic Reactions in Aqueous Media-with a Focus on Carbon-Carbon Bond Formations|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=93|issue=6|pages=2023–2035 |doi=10.1021/cr00022a004}}</ref> for various chemical reactions ([[C-H activation]]/Functionalization,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wei|first1=Chunmei|last2=Li|first2=Chao-Jun|date=2002-01-25|title=Grignard type reaction via C–H bond activation in water|journal= Green Chemistry|volume=4|issue=45|pages=39–41|doi=10.1039/B110102C}}</ref> Grignard type-reactions in water.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Li|first=Chao-Jun|date=1996-04-25|title=Aqueous Barbier-Grignard type reactions: scope, mechanism, and synthetic applications |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=52|issue=16|pages=5643–5668|doi=10.1016/0040-4020(95)01056-4}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/06/140626092917.htm |title=A breakthrough for organic reactions in water|website=ScienceDaily|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> Li originated the concepts of Aldehyde-Alkyne-Amine Coupling ([[A3 coupling reaction]]) and the [[cross dehydrogenative coupling]] (CDC Reaction, or C-H/C-H coupling, or oxidative C-H cross coupling). His work on [[gallium nitride|GaN]] [[nanowires]] and nanoparticles as [[photocatalyst]]s for the conversion of [[methane]] into [[benzene]] was covered by [[Phys.org]] in 2015, leaving prospects for [[hydrogen storage]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://phys.org/news/2015-06-simple-hydrogen-storage-solution-powered.html|title=Simple hydrogen storage solution is powered by solar energy |website=phys.org|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> Subsequently, his team showed that they were also able to convert [[methanol]] into [[ethanol]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Service|first=Robert F.|date=19 February 2019 |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/ultraviolet-light-could-provide-powerful-new-source-green-fuel |title=Ultraviolet light could provide a powerful new source of green fuel|website=Science|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190219212212/http://www.sciencemag.org/news/2019/02/ultraviolet-light-could-provide-powerful-new-source-green-fuel |archive-date=2019-02-19 }}</ref> ethylene and cyclohexane. He also made breakthroughs in using [[hydrazone]]s as organometallic surrogates in nucleophilic addition and cross-coupling,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://phys.org/news/2016-12-carbanion-analogs-derived-naturally-occurring-aldehydes.html|title=Carbanion analogs derived from naturally-occurring aldehydes|website=phys.org|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> the direct amination of phenol derivatives.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sciencetrends.com/palladium-catalyzed-deoxygenative-amination-phenols/|title=Palladium-catalyzed Deoxygenative Amination Of Phenols|website=Science Trends|date=2017-12-04|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> and the earliest report on fluorescence enhancement due to self-assembling (SAFE) in solution.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Xia |first1=Wen-Sheng|last2=Schmehl|first2=Russell H.|last3=Li|first3=Chao-Jun|date=1999-05-27|title=A highly selective fluorescent chemosensor for K+ from a bis-15-crown-5 derivative|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=121|issue=23|pages=5599–5600|doi=10.1021/ja984462c|bibcode=1999JAChS.121.5599X }}</ref>
